extracted.intended_audience: creative writers, literature students, and readers interested in literary theory
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and conceptual criteria for employing or recognizing the literary/artistic technique of defamiliarization (making the familiar strange) across narrative, language, and other artistic devices to renew perception. Covers purpose, methods (POV, diction, plot disruption), and related effects (uncanny, estrangement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / purpose of defamiliarization
rubrics_metrics.description: The artistic technique of presenting to audiences common or ordinary things in an unfamiliar or strange way so they can gain new perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: According to the Russian formalists who coined the term, it is the central concept of art and poetry; its purpose is to renew perception and to distinguish poetic from practical language. The technique aims to make audiences see 'things as they are perceived and not as they are known.' Used across 20th‑century art movements and as a tactic (e.g., culture jamming).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make objects 'unfamiliar' and prolong perception
rubrics_metrics.description: The technique of art is to make objects 'unfamiliar', to make forms difficult, to increase the difficulty and length of perception because the process of perception is an aesthetic end in itself and must be prolonged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, craft scenes, sentences, or devices that slow down recognition and comprehension so perception itself becomes the aesthetic experience; aim for impeded, extended perception rather than quick familiarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent over-automatization / deautomatize perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Defamiliarization is intended to prevent 'over-automatization,' which would cause an individual to 'function as though by formula.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create material designed to 'remove the automatism of perception' so readers must work to see and interpret; the author's purpose is to produce the vision resulting from deautomatized perception (i.e., art is created so that its perception is impeded for maximum effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of poetic (formed) language vs ordinary prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic language is fundamentally different than the language we use every day because it is more difficult to understand: 'Poetic speech is formed speech. Prose is ordinary speech – economical, easy, proper...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manipulate phonetic and lexical structures, word distribution, and characteristic thought structures to mark 'artistic trademark' — choose phrasing and sound patterns that increase perceptual effort and foreground language itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ unfamiliar or nonstandard point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Using an unusual narrator or perspective (e.g., the narrator of 'Kholstomer' is a horse) makes the content of the story seem unfamiliar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shift perspective to non-human, marginal, or unexpected viewpoints to estrange commonplace events or ideas and force re-evaluation of familiar situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use foreign languages, dialects, or 'barbarisms' in diction
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporating foreign language, dialects, or nonstandard diction can defamiliarize; literary language and everyday speech can swap places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alter diction by introducing dialect, code-switching, archaic or foreign terms, or colloquialism-cum-literary mixtures to disrupt habitual recognition of language and voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamiliarize narrative plot (syuzhet vs fabula) via structural disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: The syuzhet (plot formation) is the fabula (story matter) defamiliarized: temporal displacements, digressions, and causal disruptions (e.g., placing effects before causes) slow the reader's ability to reassemble the familiar story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use non-linear sequencing, digressions, disrupted causality, and other plot-form techniques to impede effortless reconstruction of events so the familiar story is made strange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slow reading and increase difficulty to reveal devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Defamiliarization causes both the slowing down and the increased difficulty (impeding) of reading and comprehending and an awareness of the artistic procedures (devices) causing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design passages that intentionally resist easy comprehension not as obfuscation but to make readers notice the craft — foreground technique so readers become aware of how perception is being shaped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elicit uncanny effects by making familiar strange
rubrics_metrics.description: The technique is linked to Freud's notion of the uncanny: a feeling about something being both strange and familiar rather than simply unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate subtle or supernatural elements within ordinary, quotidian settings (or vice versa) so that readers experience cognitive dissonance: something known is seen anew as eerie or uncanny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish technique from effect (defamiliarization vs estrangement/Verfremdungseffekt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defamiliarization (ostranenie) is a technique of 'making strange'; Brecht's Verfremdungseffekt ('estrangement effect') is an effect on the audience which can be caused by defamiliarization or by deliberate recontextualization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the difference between the method (stylistic/literary devices that make things strange) and the rhetorical/political effect (distance, critical awareness) — employ techniques purposefully depending on whether the goal is aesthetic estrangement or didactic/political distancing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamiliarization as production of difference (relation to différance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defamiliarization both 'differs' and 'defers' — like Derrida's différance, it draws attention to common language in a way that alters perception and forces thought about a concept in more complex terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use techniques that not only change perception but also create semantic and temporal shifts (difference and deferral), prompting re-evaluation of meanings and delaying straightforward comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad applicability across movements and media
rubrics_metrics.description: The concept has influenced 20th‑century art and theory across movements including Dadaism, postmodernism, epic theatre, science fiction, and philosophy, and is used by protest movements such as culture jamming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that defamiliarization is adaptable: it can be applied in poetry, prose, theatre, film, science fiction, visual art, and activist practices; choose media-appropriate devices (visual, verbal, performative) to achieve estrangement.
